title: Sell Mineral Rights in Sweetwater County, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Sweetwater County, WY
metaDescription: Minerals in the Green River Basin's biggest county — trona, tight gas, or Wamsutter oil? Get an offer that accounts for what's actually under your tract.
heroLead: Green River is the county seat, and Sweetwater County is the largest in Wyoming by land area — a stretch of tight gas fields, trona beds, and checkerboard railroad ground running from Rock Springs east to Wamsutter.
intro: Sweetwater County covers more ground than some states, and the mineral picture changes as you cross it. Around Rock Springs and Green River, you have a mix of Fort Union and Mesaverde gas production layered over some of the largest trona deposits in the world — trona being the raw material for soda ash, mined here on a scale most people outside Wyoming never hear about. East toward Wamsutter, the geology shifts into tight oil and gas in the Almond and Lewis formations, developed on close-spaced units similar to what you see across the border in the Great Divide Basin.

The other constant across the whole county is the checkerboard. The original Union Pacific transcontinental grant runs straight through Sweetwater County, alternating odd federal-adjacent private sections with even BLM sections mile by mile. That pattern, more than almost anywhere else in the state, decides who you deal with, what paperwork exists, and how fast a sale can close.

sections.heading: Rock Springs and Green River — gas, trona, and old title
paragraphs: The Rock Springs uplift has produced natural gas for decades, and much of the acreage around the city has been drilled and re-drilled as completion technology improved. Layered underneath a lot of that same ground is trona, mined by several companies for soda ash production — a mineral interest here can theoretically involve both oil and gas rights and solid mineral (trona) rights, and those are sometimes severed from each other separately, not only from the surface. Before we make an offer on acreage in this part of the county, we confirm exactly which mineral category your deed actually conveys.

sections.heading: Wamsutter and the tight gas fairway
paragraphs: East toward Wamsutter, the county sits over some of the most heavily developed tight gas acreage in the Rockies, close-spaced units targeting the Almond, Lewis, and Fort Union intervals. Wells here decline fast and get infilled aggressively, so a royalty history from five years ago does not tell you much about what the interest is worth today. We weight recent months heavily when pricing acreage in this part of the county rather than relying on an older average.

sections.heading: The checkerboard and split estate
paragraphs: Because the Union Pacific grant runs the length of the county, a huge share of Sweetwater County's private mineral ownership traces back to railroad patents on odd-numbered sections, with the even sections remaining federal and administered by the BLM Rock Springs field office. Surface use agreements, access, and even which regulator has jurisdiction can flip section to section. If your family's minerals came down through a ranch that straddled that pattern, split estate is common — the rancher who owned the surface often was not the same party who ended up with the minerals a generation or two later.

sections.heading: Pricing across a county this size
paragraphs: There is no single number that works for Sweetwater County — a trona-adjacent gas interest near Rock Springs, a fast-declining Wamsutter unit, and a quiet legacy fraction in between all price differently. We start with your division order or legal description, confirm the mineral type and the specific unit, and check recent production filed with the Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission before we ever put a number in front of you.

faqs.question: My deed mentions oil, gas, and 'other minerals' — does that include the trona under Rock Springs?
faqs.answer: It depends on the exact language and how the interest was originally severed. Some deeds cover solid minerals like trona, others don't. We read the deed language carefully before we price anything in that part of the county.

faqs.question: Why does my Wamsutter royalty check jump around so much?
faqs.answer: Tight gas wells in that part of the county decline quickly and get infilled with new wells fairly often, so production and pricing both move. We look at a recent stretch of checks rather than one snapshot.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my section is BLM federal or private railroad-grant land?
faqs.answer: Your legal description tells us. Odd-numbered sections in the historic railroad grant band are typically the private ones; even sections are usually federal. We confirm it against BLM Rock Springs field office and county clerk records.

faqs.question: Is Sweetwater County a good place to sell, or should I hold and keep collecting royalty?
faqs.answer: That depends on your situation and risk tolerance — we're not going to tell you what's right for your finances. What we can do is give you a real, current offer so you have an actual number to weigh against holding.

faqs.question: What paperwork do you need to get started?
faqs.answer: A division order or recent check stub is fastest. If you only have an old lease, mineral deed, or probate record, send what you have and we'll trace the rest through the courthouse in Green River.
